clue.text: Safety officer's fine when European comes back about bonus

indicators.note: the reworked word for fine wraps itself around the synonym for bonus
the European letter steps back one place within the word for fine, swapping with its neighbour

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine; here the whole word fine is used
a reward is a bonus given for good work

explanation.surface: A safety inspector is fined when a returning European is caught with a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' sends the European letter one place back, making FIEN, which 'about' wraps round the bonus. The 's of 'officer's' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire warden is the person responsible for fire safety in a building, a kind of safety officer.

clue.text: Motor manufacturer favouring Germany

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A carmaker is said to be biased towards Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford is the American car company founded by Henry Ford, a maker of motor vehicles.

clue.text: Letter I posted contains reply

indicators.note: the run of words is said to hold the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone says the letter they sent includes their response.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort, so a sharp reply in an exchange.

clue.text: Complicated work defeat him? — that's not true

indicators.note: complicated describes something tangled, so the following letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a complex task beating a man is a false claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wide of the mark is an idiom for being inaccurate, so a statement that is not true.

clue.text: Pasta — I set up a large amount first

indicators.note: first tells us that the pieces after the I in the clue come before it in the answer

parts.note: to rig up something is to set it up
a ton is a large amount, as in tons of money

explanation.surface: A cook says they arranged the pasta, having piled up a big helping first.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I' as the last letter: everything else goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a type of pasta in short ridged tubes.

clue.text: In France she procures end of John Terry perhaps

parts.note: elle is French for she

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word John

explanation.surface: In France a woman acquires the tail of the footballer John Terry.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellen Terry was a famous Victorian stage actress; the surface wants the Chelsea footballer John Terry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is the first name of the actress Ellen Terry, so Terry is an example of someone so named.

clue.text: One in flight takes favourites aback

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word for favourites reads in reverse

parts.note: teachers' pets are favourites

explanation.surface: An airline passenger is taken aback by favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one of a flight of stairs, a single unit in the series.

clue.text: Beat sailor heartlessly with cat

indicators.note: heartlessly means with the central letter taken out of the word for sailor

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
the ounce is a big cat, the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A cruel sailor beats someone with a cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to defeat them heavily, to beat them soundly.

clue.text: Somehow need priest to ordain before the event?

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unspecified way

explanation.surface: Some ritual demands a priest to officiate before an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To predestine is to determine in advance, to decree something before it happens.

clue.text: Swift attack packs little power

indicators.note: packs means holds inside, so the word for attack has the letter put in

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A fast assault carries only a little power.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms, both meaning very fast.

clue.text: Medical problem covering entire street in past

indicators.note: covering means the word for past sits around the other pieces

parts.note: gone means past, over and done
all means entire, the whole

explanation.surface: A health complaint once covered a whole street in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallstone is a hard mass formed in the gall bladder, a common medical complaint.

clue.text: Four in rubbish London suburb just get by

parts.note: scrap is waste material, rubbish

indicators.note: the Roman numeral goes inside the name of the suburb

parts.note: Ealing is a suburb of west London
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people living amid the rubbish of a London suburb barely manage.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a suburb in west London, famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape a living is an idiom for earning only just enough money to survive.

clue.text: Place for marksmen soon gathering excitedly

indicators.note: excitedly suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Sharpshooters will soon be gathering eagerly.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting range is an area where people practise firing guns at targets.

clue.text: Apply scheme to get in sought-after Swiss cheese perhaps

indicators.note: the two pieces get inside the word for sought-after

parts.note: something hot is in demand, sought-after
to use something is to apply it
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to get a coveted Swiss cheese into the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The Swiss cheese plant (Monstera) is a popular indoor plant; the surface wants Emmental.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss cheese plant, with its holey leaves, is an example of a popular indoor potted plant.

clue.text: Clear single implication

parts.note: overt means open and clear to see
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A plain single carries a clear meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a subtle extra meaning or suggestion, an implication.

clue.text: Optimistic in college course

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
a beat is the regular course a police officer patrols

explanation.surface: A student is hopeful about a college course.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful and positive, synonymous with optimistic.

clue.text: Frolic with energy in springtime — that's nonsense!

indicators.note: the two pieces sit inside the word for springtime

parts.note: May is a month in spring
a lark is a bit of fun, a frolic
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses lively spring capers as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarkey is informal for foolish talk, meaning nonsense.

clue.text: Coterie including private group

indicators.note: including means the word for coterie holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: a set is a coterie, a social group
PTE is the army abbreviation for private

explanation.surface: An exclusive circle includes a private group.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a group of seven, typically musicians.

clue.text: Nothing penned by playwright makes suggestion

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed in the playwright's name, as in a pen

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright
O is the zero shape, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A dramatist writing nothing gives a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a hint or tip, a suggestion of what to do.

clue.text: Brought about no harm at gruelling event

indicators.note: brought about suggests the letters are turned around and made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone at a punishing race did no damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a race of over 26 miles, a notoriously exhausting event.

clue.text: Place to meet a non-governmental organisation in small building

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for small building

parts.note: a hut is a small simple building
NGO is the abbreviation for non-governmental organisation

explanation.surface: A charity has its meeting place in a little shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangout is a place where people habitually spend time together.

clue.text: I remained still in poverty — it was Thatcher's policy

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the word for poverty

parts.note: privation is lack of necessities, poverty
to sit is to remain still; sat is past tense

explanation.surface: Someone recalls staying put in hardship under Thatcher's policies.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher, UK Prime Minister 1979-90, sold off state industries.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling state-owned industries to the market was the defining economic policy of Margaret Thatcher's government.

clue.text: A limo crashed in Grand Prix venue

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.definitionFit: Imola in Italy hosts a Formula One circuit that has staged Grand Prix races.

clue.text: Goddess — one affectionate way to address girl

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
sis, short for sister, is a fond way to address a girl

explanation.surface: A deity is described as a fond way to speak to a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egyptian religion.

clue.text: Fuel additive in tank, I conk out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Something added to the petrol tank means the engine stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: To conk out is to break down; 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiknock agent is added to petrol to stop engines knocking.

clue.text: Actor smooths things over

definitions.meaning: Jeremy ... is an English film actor
presses clothes with a hot appliance to flatten creases

explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is a famous actor, and to iron clothes is to smooth out their creases.

clue.text: Expression used in 'Mastermind'

explanation.surface: A phrase appears on the television quiz show.

clue.text: Sit angrily suffering sore throat

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are in a bad state, thrown into disorder
